0.body:
# Furlong — Quick Start

*1–6 players · 30–45 minutes · Everything you need for your first race. The rulebook settles
anything this sheet doesn't cover, and wins if the two ever disagree.*

## The idea

You are a jockey. **Six horses always race**: each player rides one, and riderless horses make up
the rest of the field. **Whoever is furthest past the finish line wins.**

Every turn you play one card, and the card is how hard you ask your horse to run. Run hard now and
your deck fills with **Exhaust**, dead cards that clog your hand later. Run easy and you **bank
Sprints**, the big cards that win the stretch. When to spend is the whole game.

## Set up your first race

The first race is **Basic** on **the Furlong Oval** at **120 spaces**.

1. **The board.** Lay the chute strip on the Oval's home straight, lanes on lanes, with its
   **WIRE END** exactly on the wire. The field starts on the strip's **START 120** line.
2. **Six horses.** Each player takes a horse and its mat. The horses nobody rides run
   **riderless** (see *Riderless horses* below).
3. **Posts.** Shuffle the six post-position cards, deal one to every horse (riderless ones too)
   and turn them over. That is the lane each horse starts in, on the START 120 line.
4. **Decks.** Each player takes their horse's own ten cards, stamped with its name (its mat lists
   them). Every horse's mix is different: that mix is its **running style** (see below).
5. **The shared piles.** Shuffle the **Sprint deck** and set it face down in its well in the
   infield, with the **Exhaust** pile in the well beside it.
6. **The bot deck** (if any horse is riderless). Shuffle it and put **five cards back in the box
   unseen**. That is the Normal level at the 120.
7. **Draw.** Each player shuffles their deck and draws a **hand of 4**.

## The cards

| Card | Moves | Then |
|---|---|---|
| **Settle** | 5 | **Bank** a Sprint |
| **Cruise** | 6 | **Bank** a Sprint |
| **Pace** | 7 | nothing |
| **Push** | 8 | take **1 Exhaust** into your discard pile |
| **Drive** | 9 | take **1 Exhaust**, shuffled into your draw pile |
| **Sprint** | 10–12 | take **3 Exhaust**; the Sprint is then removed from the game |
| **Exhaust** | 3 | nothing |

**Bank a Sprint:** move the top card of the shared Sprint deck into your discard pile, face down,
**without looking at it**. You find out what it's worth (10, 11 or 12) when you draw it later.

## Running styles

Every deck is **5 Pace, 1 Sprint 11** and **4 style cards**: Push and Drive **press**, Settle and
Cruise **bank**. The mix is how your horse likes to run.

| Style | Style cards | How it wins |
|---|---|---|
| **Front-runner** | 3 press, 1 bank | Goes hard from the gate and tries to lead all the way. |
| **Stalker** | 2 press, 2 bank | Keeps in touch, then picks its moment. |
| **Closer** | 1 press, 3 bank | Banks early, then unloads a barrage in the stretch. |

## A round

1. **Set.** Everyone at once, in secret: from your hand of 4, **set one card face down** (this is
   your move), **carry one** card for next round, and **discard the rest**.
2. **Bots.** If any horse is riderless, flip the top bot card now.
3. **Run, front to back.** The horse furthest along goes first (if level, the inner lane goes
   first). On your turn: **flip your card, make your whole move, apply the card's effect**, then
   **draw straight back up to 4** (your carried card counts). Then the next horse goes.

You never see what the horses behind you set until they run.

## Moving

- **Your card's number is your budget.** Each space forward costs 1. Your **first lane change is
  free**; each one after that costs 1.
- **Curves.** If your move touches a bend at all, pay its **curve penalty once**, at the rate of the
  **widest lane you were in** during the move. On the Oval, lanes 1–3 pay nothing, lanes 4–5 pay 1
  and lane 6 pays 2. The board shows it: the denser the hatching, the more a lane costs. Nothing is
  ever charged past the wire.
- **A horse is two spaces long** (its head and its tail) and **solid**: you can't move into or
  through another horse. Go around it, or **hold** where you are, which costs nothing.
- **Slipstream.** If you stop with **one or two empty spaces** directly behind another horse in
  your lane, you move forward free to tuck in behind it. The wire does not stop it: a slipstream
  can take you over the line.

## Finishing

- On the 120 you cross the wire once as you come off the chute strip. **The finish is the next
  time you reach it**, a lap later. The numbers along the rail count the spaces you have left.
  Once every horse has crossed the wire, lift the strip off.
- Your horse **finishes** when its head reaches the line, but **keep moving**: spend every point
  you have left.
- Horses that finish in the same round are placed by **who ended furthest past the line**, then
  by the inner lane. **First place wins.** Lead finished horses off the track at the end of the
  round.

## Your deck

- **Your discard pile is face down, and nobody looks at it, including you.**
- Draw pile empty? Shuffle your discard pile into a new one. Nothing left anywhere? Take one
  Exhaust from the shared pile.
- You can carry **only one** card: a Sprint for the stretch, *or* the card you want to run next,
  never both.

## Riderless horses

A riderless horse has no hand and makes no choices. Each round, after everyone has set, **flip one
bot card**. Each riderless horse moves the number in **its own row**, on its turn in running order.

- Use the **first-pass** number until the bot deck runs out. Then shuffle every flipped bot card
  into a new deck and use the **kick** number for the rest of the race.
- A bot takes whichever line leaves its head **furthest up the track**, after paying for lane
  changes and curves and counting any slipstream. If two lines tie, it takes the inner one.

## Tips for the first race

- **Don't carry your Sprint early.** The wire is far away; let it go round and keep the carry slot
  for the card you want next.
- **Bank through the middle of the race, sprint late.** A Sprint's 3 Exhaust rarely comes back round
  before the wire if you fire it in the stretch.
- **The rail is short, but a wake can be worth more.** A slipstream is free ground; tucking in
  behind a horse can beat holding the inside.

## After your first race

- **Advanced:** draft traits and special cards before the race, under the Going (the weather and
  track conditions).
- Other boards and distances, two-player and solo rules: see the rulebook.

ObjectStates.Name: Custom_Tile
ObjectStates.Description: Right-click > States to switch to Three Sisters: the Sprint deck and Exhaust follow to its wells. Chute strip on the home straight for the 100 and 120 (WIRE END on the wire).
ObjectStates.LuaScript:
-- Furlong (tabletop-simulator/export.mjs): when the board switches, the shared piles follow to this board's wells.
local MINE = { { x = -2.0374, z = 0 }, { x = 2.0374, z = 0 } }
local OTHER = { { x = -4.3278, z = 0.8957 }, { x = -0.253, z = 0.8957 } }
function onLoad()
  self.setPosition({ 0, 1, 0 })
  self.setRotation({ 0, 180, 0 })
  self.setScale({ 8.4742, 1, 8.4742 })
  Wait.frames(function()
    for i, w in ipairs(OTHER) do
      for _, o in ipairs(getAllObjects()) do
        if o.type == "Deck" or o.type == "Card" then
          local p = o.getPosition()
          if (p.x - w.x) ^ 2 + (p.z - w.z) ^ 2 < 1.5 ^ 2 then
            o.setPositionSmooth({ MINE[i].x, p.y + 0.5, MINE[i].z }, false, true)
          end
        end
      end
    end
  end, 10)
end
